sections.name: Crude Oil & Distillation
sections.description: Crude receipt and assay plus atmospheric/vacuum cut characterization: API gravity & density (ASTM D5002/D1298), TBP and physical distillation (D86/D7169/D2892), salt content (D3230), water by Karl Fischer/distillation (D6304/D4006), BS&W, RVP (D323/D5191), H2S & RSH mercaptans, sulfur (D4294/D2622), TAN (D664) and pour point (D97).

sections.name: Gasoline / Mogas Chemistry
sections.description: Finished motor gasoline (Premium 95 / Regular 91) testing: research & motor octane RON/MON (D2699/D2700), PIONA & oxygenates by GC (D6730/D5599/D4815), benzene & aromatics (D3606/D5580), RVP (D5191), distillation (D86), sulfur (D5453), lead (D3237), gum (D381) and oxidation stability (D525).

sections.name: Naphtha, Reformate & Aromatics
sections.description: Naphtha feeds/reformate and aromatics-complex streams (benzene, toluene, mixed & para-xylene): detailed PIONA/PINA by GC (D6729/D5134), bromine index (D2710), non-aromatic & purity by GC (D7504/D3797/D5917), color (D1209 APHA), acid wash color, total chloride and sulfur speciation (D3961).

sections.name: Middle Distillates (Jet / Kero & Diesel / Gasoil)
sections.description: Jet A-1/kerosene and automotive diesel/gasoil: flash point (D93), freeze point (D2386), smoke point (D1322), cetane index/number (D4737/D613), cloud & CFPP (D5773/D6371), pour point (D97), cold filter/lubricity HFRR (D6079), distillation (D86/D2887), sulfur (D5453) and FAME content (EN 14078).

sections.name: Fuel Oil, Asphalt & Lube Base Oils
sections.description: Heavy fuel oil/HSFO bunker, paving bitumen/asphalt and lube base oils: kinematic & dynamic viscosity (D445/D7042), CCAI, asphaltenes (D6560), MCRT/CCR (D4530), penetration & softening point (D5/D36), ductility, Sara fractions, viscosity index (D2270), CCS and acid/base number (D664/D2896).

sections.name: Refinery Gas & LPG
sections.description: Fuel gas, LPG and propane/butane streams: refinery & natural gas composition by GC (D1945/D2163), calorific value/Wobbe (D3588), vapor pressure of LPG (D1267/D6897), residue & evaporation (D2158), total & speciated sulfur (D6667/D5504), H2S by stain tube (D2420) and copper corrosion (D1838).

sections.name: Environmental, Water & Utilities
sections.description: Boiler feed/cooling water, steam condensate, effluent/wastewater and stack/ambient air: pH & conductivity (D1293/D1125), TDS/TSS, hardness, silica, phosphate, dissolved O2, oil-in-water (D7066), COD/BOD, total sulfur & H2S in gas, and trace metals by ICP (D1976).

sections.name: QA/QC & Calibration
sections.description: Cross-section quality unit: control-chart QC check samples, certified reference materials/CRM verification, instrument calibration & verification (balances, GC/ICP/XRF, density meters), method validation, proficiency-test/ASTM ILCP round robins, blanks/spikes and uncertainty budgets.

kpis.name: On-Time Sample Turnaround %
kpis.description: Percentage of samples authorised within their target TAT (LOGIN_DATE to AUTHORIZED_DATE) by GROUP_NAME priority class. Crude assay (CRUDE_DIST) target 24-48 h; routine MOGAS/DIESEL release tests 8 h; LPG/gas (GAS_LPG) and environmental water (ENV_WATER) within their SLA windows.

kpis.name: First-Pass Spec Compliance %
kpis.description: Share of results passing within ASTM/IP spec limits on first entry without retest or repeat, across release tests such as D2622 sulfur, D5191 RVP, D613 cetane, D86 distillation and D4294 sulfur. Reflects right-first-time quality of analysts and instruments.

kpis.name: Instrument Uptime %
kpis.description: Available (in-service) hours divided by scheduled hours from INSTRUMENTS1_LOG, across critical analysers: Agilent 7890 GC, Thermo Antek/XOS Sindie sulfur, Anton Paar SVM3001 viscometer, Metrohm KF titrators, Herzog/Tanaka distillation and flash units.

kpis.name: Calibration Overdue Count
kpis.description: Number of instruments or reference standards past their calibration/verification due date (e.g. GC retention check, sulfur D6299 control, density U-tube, thermometer ITS-90 verification). Each overdue item blocks accredited (ISO/IEC 17025) result release.

kpis.name: Retest Rate %
kpis.description: Percentage of results requiring re-analysis (REPEAT/RETEST flag in LIMS) due to QC failure, out-of-control charts, ASTM repeatability breach, or analyst entry error. Lower is better; a key driver of TAT and reagent cost.

kpis.name: Off-Spec Product Rate %
kpis.description: Percentage of finished-product release batches (Mogas 91/95, EN590 Diesel, Jet A-1, LPG, fuel oil, sulphur) failing one or more certificate-of-quality specs and quarantined or re-blended. Directly tied to refinery giveaway and reprocessing.

kpis.name: Samples Logged Per Day
kpis.description: Mean number of samples logged into LIMS per working day (COUNT of SAMPLE by LOGIN_DATE), aggregated across all sections. Tracks lab workload and is the baseline for staffing and the sample-volume forecast.

kpis.name: Mean Turnaround Time (TAT)
kpis.description: Average elapsed hours from sample login to final authorisation, weighted across sections. The headline responsiveness metric reported to operations and blending planners.

kpis.name: QC Control Within Limits %
kpis.description: Percentage of QC/check-standard results falling within Westgard / ASTM D6299 control-chart limits (mean +/- 2-3 SD) for assays running internal reference materials. Indicates analytical method stability.

kpis.name: Proficiency Test (PT) Z-Score Pass Rate %
kpis.description: Share of inter-laboratory proficiency-testing results (e.g. ASTM ILCP, IIS crude assay round-robins) with |z| <= 2, evidencing accredited measurement competence for the ISO/IEC 17025 scope.

kpis.name: Result Backlog (Pending Authorisation)
kpis.description: Count of completed results awaiting supervisor authorisation in LIMS at end of shift. A rising backlog signals review bottlenecks that silently breach TAT even when bench work is done.

alerts.name: Off-Spec Sulfur (Diesel/Mogas)
alerts.rationale: EN590 / Euro V road diesel and Mogas have a 10 mg/kg (ppm) max total sulfur by ASTM D2622 / D5453. A result above 10 ppm means the batch cannot be certified for the ULSD/Mogas pool and must be quarantined and re-blended before export from the refinery.

alerts.name: Jet A-1 Flash Point Below Limit
alerts.rationale: ASTM D56/D3828 flash point for Jet A-1 (DEF STAN 91-091 / ASTM D1655) must be >= 38 C for safe handling. A sub-38 C reading flags a volatile/contaminated jet batch and an immediate aviation-fuel safety hold.

alerts.name: Mogas RVP Above Seasonal Limit
alerts.rationale: Reid Vapour Pressure (ASTM D5191) drives evaporative emissions and vapour lock. Summer refinery gasoline must stay below the seasonal RVP cap (~60 kPa); a breach means the blend is off-spec and risks tank venting losses.

alerts.name: Instrument Downtime Spike
alerts.rationale: More than 4 unscheduled downtime hours in 24 h on a critical analyser (GC sulfur, distillation, viscometer) from INSTRUMENTS1_LOG starves the release queue and cascades into TAT breaches; triggers maintenance escalation and sample rerouting.

alerts.name: TAT SLA Breach
alerts.rationale: When more than 10% of in-progress samples have exceeded their section TAT target, the lab is missing its operations SLA. Early warning lets the supervisor reprioritise release-critical product samples ahead of routine work.

alerts.name: Calibration / Verification Overdue
alerts.rationale: Any instrument or reference standard past its calibration due date invalidates results under ISO/IEC 17025. Even one overdue item must block result authorisation, so the threshold is zero tolerance.

alerts.name: Reagent / Standard Below Reorder Level
alerts.rationale: Critical consumables (Karl Fischer reagent, certified sulfur standards, GC carrier gas, cetane reference fuels) dropping below 20% of reorder point risk a method stoppage; raises a procurement alert tied to the inventory forecast.

alerts.name: QC Control Out-of-Range (Westgard)
alerts.rationale: A check-standard result beyond +/-3 SD (ASTM D6299 / Westgard 1-3s rule) indicates the analytical method is out of statistical control. All results since the last in-control QC are suspect and must be held pending re-calibration and re-analysis.

vision_use_cases.name: ASTM Colour & Appearance Grading
vision_use_cases.description: Camera/colourimeter images of product samples are graded against ASTM D1500 (dark oils, diesel, fuel oil), Saybolt ASTM D156 (jet, light naphtha) and D6045 visual colour scales, plus haze/clarity and visible water or sediment. The model returns a colour number and clear-and-bright pass/fail, auto-populating the LIMS appearance field and flagging off-colour or hazy batches for review.

vision_use_cases.name: Chromatogram Peak QC
vision_use_cases.description: GC/SimDis and PIONA chromatograms (D2887 simulated distillation, D6730/D5134 detailed hydrocarbon analysis, RGA refinery-gas) are screened by a vision model for baseline drift, peak tailing/fronting, co-elution, retention-time shift versus the reference standard, and missing internal-standard peaks. Bad runs are flagged for retest before results are authorised.

vision_use_cases.name: Crude / Sediment Image Classification
vision_use_cases.description: Images of crude-oil and bottoms samples, BS&W (water-and-sediment) centrifuge tubes (ASTM D4007), and filtration pads are classified for emulsion layers, sediment/water content band, asphaltene precipitation and free-water presence. Supports crude-assay intake (CRUDE_DIST) and tank-receipt acceptance decisions.

vision_use_cases.name: Corrosion-Coupon Image Scoring
vision_use_cases.description: Macro images of copper-strip corrosion strips (ASTM D130 for gasoline/jet/LPG), silver-strip tests, and metal corrosion coupons are scored against the standard rating chart (1a-4c) and for pitting, tarnish and scale. Automates a subjective visual test, giving a repeatable corrosion classification for LPG/MOGAS/jet release.

vision_use_cases.name: Gauge / Meter OCR Reading
vision_use_cases.description: OCR/vision reads analogue and digital displays on bench instruments and utilities, manual thermometers, pressure gauges, hydrometer (API gravity) scales, distillation temperatures and balance readouts, transcribing them straight into LIMS result fields. Eliminates manual transcription errors and timestamps the reading for the audit trail.

vision_use_cases.name: Distillation Flask Boil Image Monitoring
vision_use_cases.description: Video frames of the ASTM D86 / D1160 distillation flask are analysed to detect the initial boiling point (first drop), bumping/foaming, flooding, decomposition smoke, and consistent drop rate, cross-checking the recorded IBP/FBP curve. Flags abnormal boils that would invalidate the distillation result for naphtha, mogas, jet and diesel.

issues.problem: ASTM D4492 is 'Standard Test Method for Benzene Content of Cyclic Products by Gas Chromatography' - it determines benzene AS AN IMPURITY in other cyclic products (e.g. toluene, cyclohexane). It is NOT the method for assaying the purity of a benzene product stream. Purity of refined benzene is determined by ASTM D2360 (trace impurities by capillary GC) or ASTM D4307, with overall purity by D850/GC area%.
issues.correction: Change method for benzene product purity to ASTM D4734 / D2360 (impurities by GC) reporting purity by difference, or report purity via ASTM D850 distillation + GC. Keep D4492 only if the intent is 'benzene-in-toluene' impurity. The FFAP capillary GC-FID instrument is appropriate for the corrected method.

issues.problem: ASTM D3797 is 'Analysis of o-Xylene by Gas Chromatography' (xylene-specific), not a toluene purity method. It is mismatched to the toluene product.
issues.correction: Use ASTM D5917 (trace impurities in monocyclic aromatics by GC with external calibration) or ASTM D2360, reporting toluene purity by difference. Instrument (capillary FFAP GC-FID) is fine.

issues.item: MOGAS-91 - Total Aromatics (ASTM D5769) typical_mean 28.5 vol%
issues.problem: ASTM D5769 reports aromatics in mass% (it is a GC-MS method calibrated by mass), not vol%. The unit 'vol%' is inconsistent with the method's native output. Also for a 91 RON regular gasoline, 28.5 vol% total aromatics is on the high side relative to the olefin/octane balance but is acceptable; the unit is the real defect.
issues.correction: Either report in mass% (D5769 native) or, if vol% aromatics is required against the typical EN228-style 35 vol% limit, use ASTM D6839 (GC-PIONA, vol%) or D1319. Align unit with chosen method.

issues.item: MOGAS-91 - Distillation FBP spec_max 215 / MOGAS-95 FBP spec_max 210 with T50 only
issues.problem: Not physically wrong, but the gasoline distillation set is internally incomplete/odd: an FBP max of 215 deg C is higher than the typical worldwide gasoline FBP limit of 210 deg C and the D86 FBP residue/E70/E100/E150 fractional-evaporated points are missing. Minor realism gap, not an impossibility.
issues.correction: Tighten MOGAS-91 FBP spec_max to 210 deg C to match MOGAS-95 and EN228/typical refinery limits; consider adding E70 (20-48 vol%) and E100 (46-71 vol%) evaporated points for authenticity. Low priority.

issues.item: LPG-C3C4 - Residual Matter / Volatile Residue (ASTM D2158) unit 'mL'
issues.problem: ASTM D2158 'Residues in Liquefied Petroleum (LP) Gases' reports the oil residue as mL (residue on evaporation) AND the end point of the residue; the residue limit is typically expressed in mL per 100 mL (e.g. 0.05 mL/100 mL). Bare 'mL' with spec_max 0.05 is ambiguous but the residue-evaporation apparatus and method are correct.
issues.correction: Express unit as 'mL/100 mL' (e.g. spec_max 0.05 mL/100 mL) to remove ambiguity. Method and instrument are correct.

issues.problem: ASTM D2163 'Determination of Hydrocarbons in Liquefied Petroleum (LP) Gases and Propane/Propene Mixtures by Gas Chromatography' covers C1 through C5+ components. The descriptor and the analyzer ('Refinery Gas Analyser GC-TCD/FID') are appropriate; minor: D2163 is the LPG-specific GC method (correct), so no method error, only the typical_mean of 60 vol% for an unnamed single component is meaningless without specifying which component (e.g. C3).
issues.correction: Specify the reported component (e.g. propane content ~ a given vol%) or report the method as a composition profile rather than a single mean. No method/instrument change needed.

issues.item: PROP-COM / LPG-C3C4 Vapour Pressure (ASTM D1267) vs commercial spec
issues.problem: ASTM D1267 (LPG gauge vapour pressure) is correct and the apparatus is correct, but using a 1430 kPa cap for a C3/C4 MIX (LPG-C3C4) is the propane limit. A propane/butane mix would normally carry a lower combined-product VP limit; 1430 kPa is really the commercial-propane figure.
issues.correction: For the LPG-C3C4 commercial mix, set the VP limit per the actual product grade (commercial propane 1434 kPa, commercial butane 485 kPa, P/B mix ~ per D1835 grade). Keep 1430 kPa only for the pure/commercial-propane stream (PROP-COM).

issues.item: BENZENE - Density at 15 C spec 882-886 kg/m3 typical_mean 884
issues.problem: Benzene density is conventionally specified at 20 C (~876.5 kg/m3) or 15 C (~884 kg/m3). The 882-886 kg/m3 window at 15 C is physically correct (~884). No error - flagged only to confirm. Genuine concern: typical_std 0.6 with a 4 kg/m3 window is realistic. This item is OK.
issues.correction: No change required; benzene at 15 C ~884 kg/m3 is correct. (Included for completeness.)

verification.overall_assessment: The dataset is largely authentic to refinery petroleum testing - real ASTM methods, realistic means/std-devs, and correct instruments for most physical/chemical tests (octane via CFR engine, RVP via Grabner/Setavap, density via Anton Paar DMA, sulfur via D5453 UV fluorescence and D6667 for gas, distillation via Herzog/PAC OptiDist). The clearest defects are in the AROMATICS PURITY block: ASTM D4492 (benzene-in-cyclic-products) is wrongly used to assay BENZENE product purity, and ASTM D3797 (o-xylene analysis) is wrongly used for TOLUENE purity - both should use the trace-impurity-by-GC methods (D2360/D5917/D4734) with purity by difference. Secondary issues are unit conventions: D5769 aromatics are natively mass% not vol%, and D2158 LPG residue should read mL/100 mL. The propane vapour-pressure limit (1430 kPa) is mis-applied to the C3/C4 mixed-LPG grade. Distillation realism for gasolines could be improved by adding E70/E100/E150 evaporated points and harmonising the FBP limit to 210 deg C. None of the core physics (densities, vapour pressures, octane ranges, sulfur limits) is impossible; the corrections are method/unit/grade alignment rather than gross errors.
